answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to post a refundable stake before it can trade, with the stake slashed if peers attest fraud. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital each time, like planting a willow in a meadow: one tree is cheap, a whole forest is not. Honest agents earn their stake back plus fees, while a burst of throwaway identities, bright but brief as a comet, burns money faster than it can steal value.
